solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A civil rector sadly becoming too judgmental

indicators.note: sadly suggests the words are in a sorry, disordered state, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman with a civil manner has unfortunately become censorious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges the twelve letters of A CIVIL RECTOR; 'becoming' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being excessively quick to find fault is exactly what too judgmental describes.

clue.text: It's alive, moving! Get going!

indicators.note: moving says the letters shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as the letters I, T, S

explanation.surface: A Frankenstein-style cry that the creature lives, followed by a command to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges the letters of IT'S ALIVE; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To vitalise is to give life or energy to, so the imperative urges something into action.

clue.text: Some of our ideas for a jaunt?

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Perhaps we have a few thoughts about an outing.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for a jaunt' as the definition, but 'for a' is a link: the noun jaunt alone swaps for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A short trip for pleasure on a horse or in a car is a jaunt.

clue.text: Army unit's American soldier joining this person in charge

indicators.note: in says the pair sits inside the word for charge

parts.note: a rental is the charge for hiring something

indicators.note: joining says the soldier and the setter are linked side by side

parts.note: GI is the usual term for a US soldier
the setter refers to themself as this person, giving me

explanation.surface: A US serviceman teams up with the speaker who commands a military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts GIME inside RENTAL. The definition is adjectival: 'Army unit's' means belonging to a regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to a regiment, a unit of the army, is described as regimental.

clue.text: Kid eating 'uge pile that is on the meal table?

definitions.text: that is on the meal table

indicators.note: eating says one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a tot is a small child
a huge pile is a heap; with the H dropped, as in 'uge for huge, it is eap

explanation.surface: A child scoffs a vast mound of food, spoken in dropped-aitch dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'uge mimics a dropped-aitch accent, the hint that heap loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot for brewing and pouring tea is set on the table at mealtimes.

clue.text: Copper is at home and wife's finishing cooking

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
in means at home

indicators.note: finishing points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A policeman is home and his wife is completing the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal. 'finishing' takes E, the last letter of wife's.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of cooking, especially a national one, is a cuisine.

clue.text: They will get at the truth — i.e. secret told after torturing

definitions.text: They will get at the truth

indicators.note: torturing twists the letters out of their order

explanation.surface: Interrogators extract a secret through torture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torturing' is the anagram signal; 'after' is merely a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Polygraph machines are used to try to determine whether someone is telling the truth.

clue.text: Very keen to get muck reduced on top of house

indicators.note: on top of says, in this down answer, the first piece sits above the second
reduced says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: gunge is British slang for sticky dirt

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly reduces the dirt piled on the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts GUNGE to GUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: Gung-ho describes someone unthinkingly enthusiastic, very eager.

clue.text: Get rid of French author, tearing page right out

indicators.note: tearing, together with out, says letters are ripped away from the author's name
out completes tearing ... out, the instruction to remove letters

parts.note: Marcel Proust wrote In Search of Lost Time

explanation.surface: Someone wants to dispose of a French writer's book by ripping out pages.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P and R from PROUST to leave the answer; 'tearing ... out' is split around the letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject or expel someone is to get rid of them.

clue.text: Make absolute assertions as scoundrel — friend is being taken in

parts.note: a dog is an old word for a rotten fellow

indicators.note: being taken in says one piece is swallowed inside another

parts.note: mate is British slang for a friend

explanation.surface: Someone pronounces dogmatically like a rogue while a pal is being fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being taken in' makes MATISE; DOG for a rotter is old-fashioned, and 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To state opinions as if they were unquestionable truths is to lay down the law arrogantly.

clue.text: Suffered financially and was uncomfortable in Oxford maybe

definitions.meaning: an Oxford is a lace-up shoe, and tight shoes squeeze the feet

explanation.surface: Someone at Oxford University struggled with money and discomfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the university city but is a style of shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to experience hardship, especially lack of money, and literally describes a tight shoe.

clue.text: Socialist finding heavenly types wrong-headed

indicators.note: wrong-headed says the first letter of the word is the wrong one and must be changed

parts.note: angels are beings from heaven

explanation.surface: A left-winger discovers that some angelic beings are misguided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong-headed' swaps the opening A of ANGELS for E.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels co-wrote The Communist Manifesto with Marx, so he is a famous socialist thinker.

clue.text: A little creature, one day buried, to become a fossil

indicators.note: buried says one piece is placed deep inside another

parts.note: a mite is a tiny arachnid
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday, a single day of the week

explanation.surface: A small animal, dead and interred, eventually turns to stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buried' makes MMONITE; 'to become a' are link words, and the surface's buried creature turning to stone is exactly how fossils form.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonites are coiled extinct molluscs whose shells are among the commonest fossils found.

clue.text: Drunk diner, one moving quickly around, becoming more affectionate?

indicators.note: around says the fast mover encloses the scrambled letters

parts.note: a flier is someone or something that travels fast

indicators.note: drunk suggests the word is reeling, so its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A tipsy restaurant customer, with a sprinter around, grows warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' makes RIEND, which 'around' encloses. The question mark notes drink's tendency to make people affable.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendlier means kinder and warmer towards others, more affectionate.

clue.text: Stealing from employer? Naughty to grin about that

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the word for employer
naughty says the letters misbehave and fall out of order

parts.note: one who employs or makes use of something is a user

explanation.surface: An employee who pilfers from the boss is cheekily told to smile about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employer' looks like a boss but means one who employs, a USER; 'that' points back to it, and 'Naughty' scrambles TO GRIN around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousering is British slang for pocketing money, often dishonestly, so it is a form of stealing.

clue.text: Monk's rosary component, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is to be judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: a bead is one of the small balls strung on a rosary

explanation.surface: A monk's string of prayer beads seems to be the topic of conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': 'Monk is rosary component, we hear'. The Venerable Bede was an Anglo-Saxon monk and historian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable Bede was a Northumbrian monk who wrote an early history of the English church.

clue.text: This person cried stupidly about love being 'ordinary'

parts.note: the setter calls themself this person, giving me

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go around the zero
stupidly suggests the word is jumbled foolishly

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: The setter wept foolishly over a love described as average.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' turns CRIED into DICRE, and 'about' puts it round O; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediocre means of only average quality, not special.

clue.text: Army needs something to give uplift, having lost heart

indicators.note: having lost heart says the central letter is dropped

parts.note: a hoist is a device for lifting loads

explanation.surface: Discouraged soldiers need a morale booster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost heart' removes the middle I of HOIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a large multitude, in old usage specifically an army.

clue.text: Short recreational activity organised? See it at Highland Games

indicators.note: Short says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: sport is activity for recreation
ran means organised, as in ran an event

explanation.surface: A brief game is arranged and watched at a Scottish sports gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts SPORT to SPOR. A sporran is the pouch worn on the front of a Scottish kilt, seen at Highland Games, Scottish athletics gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: Highland dress, with kilt and sporran, is widely worn at Scottish Highland Games.

clue.text: Feast is meagre — Lent possibly?

indicators.note: possibly hints that these words might be arranged otherwise, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a Lenten meal makes a poor banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MEAGRE and LENT together; 'is' is a link. Lent is the Christian season of fasting, ironic beside a feast.
explanation.definitionFit: A regalement is a lavish entertainment of food and drink, a banquet.

clue.text: Important? Not leader getting pretty old

indicators.note: Not leader says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: weighty means important or serious

explanation.surface: A significant figure, not in charge, has aged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not leader' removes W from WEIGHTY; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An age of four score years is reasonably considered pretty old.

clue.text: Comment when singer Billy J. gets upset?

indicators.note: gets upset in a down clue says the name is turned upside down

parts.note: Billy J. Kramer was a 1960s Liverpool pop singer with the Dakotas

explanation.surface: Someone asks what to say when a 1960s pop singer is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets upset' reverses KRAMER; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is an observation or comment made in speech.

clue.text: Goes on making money from enterprise

definitions.meaning: to continue or advance, verb sense
takings or income produced by a sale or venture, noun sense

explanation.surface: A business continues making a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb meaning advances and the noun for income from a sale or event.

clue.text: Performer in the belfry — guest brought in by team?

definitions.meaning: an outsider fielded by a side, often illicitly, as if a regular member

explanation.surface: A bell-tower performer is drafted in as an outsider for a side.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the looser second sense: a player smuggled into a team under false pretences.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a bell-puller in a tower and an impostor slipped into a competing side.

clue.text: Rachel's sister in meadow lying on top of hay

indicators.note: lying on says, in this down answer, the first piece rests above the next

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for meadow

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A biblical sister lies in a field on top of hay.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Leah is Rachel's elder sister, both wives of Jacob; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Genesis, Leah is Rachel's elder sister, married first to Jacob.

clue.text: A bishop captured by member of indigenous tribe? That'll make a story

indicators.note: captured by says the first pieces are held inside the next

parts.note: a native is an original inhabitant of a land
RR, Right Reverend, is the title abbreviation for a bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman seized by tribespeople provides material for a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: RR (Right Reverend) is a bishop's title; 'captured by' encloses ARR, and 'That'll make a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of connected events, which is what a story is.

clue.text: Civility depleted at the core in business community

indicators.note: depleted at the core says the middle of the word is drained away, keeping the ends

explanation.surface: Politeness has worn thin among people in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depleted at the core' removes VILI from the centre of CIVILITY. The City is London's financial district, so the word also names that business world.
explanation.definitionFit: London's financial district and its firms are called the City, a business community.

clue.text: Piece of cloth worker presented to King and Queen first

parts.note: a hand is a manual labourer
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the conventional abbreviation for the Queen
chief means first or foremost, as in chief concern

explanation.surface: A labourer hands a piece of fabric to the monarchs ahead of anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presented to' is a link joining HAND to the royal pieces; 'first' is not a placement instruction but the synonym CHIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A handkerchief is a small square of fabric for wiping the nose.
